The five amphetamine estimates are not identified in the article, and the methods record methamphetamine, amphetamine and cocaine psychoses together as stimulant-induced. No categorical study feature predicted transition at the review's Bonferroni threshold for subgroup comparisons (P < .01). In meta-regression, for which no threshold is stated, length of follow-up (P = .3433) and percentage followed up (β −1.716, P = .0785; lower transition with more complete follow-up) were not associated. Older cohorts had lower transition (β −0.050, P = .0286), which the review reports as a finding and suggests may be ecological. Few studies recorded the amount of use before the episode, comorbid substance use disorders or continued use; most diagnoses came from registers or routine care (research interviews in 8 studies, 127 people). The authors state that substance-induced is used by convention, not as a presumed causal link.
